clue.text: Lock put on for secure place

indicators.note: one piece is placed onto the end of the other, so the lock follows the little word

parts.note: taken as written
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Someone fits a lock to keep a place safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a door fitting but means a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold or castle is a secure place, built to be defended.

clue.text: Old rhyme about house which may be outside Oxford

indicators.note: the rhyme goes around the house, enclosing it

parts.note: a rhyme is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: An old poem about a house somewhere near the university city of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a laced leather shoe, not the city; a galosh pulled over it goes outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber overshoe is worn over an ordinary shoe such as an Oxford brogue to keep it dry.

clue.text: Renegade with instructions to get Territorials' leading officer

annotationWithheld.why: Renegade with instructions to get Territorials' leading officer: the clue is sound, a reverse clue (TURN COAT read as an order gives TAOC, TA's OC), but its only parse is a reverse reading over a 5-word phrase, which the reversePhrase check refuses; no charade or other tree honestly gives the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Renegade with instructions to get Territorials' leading officer

clue.text: Repeated sound of a screech owl

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters belonging to the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Describing the noise a screech owl makes.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'screech' and the start of 'owl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation that comes back off a surface is a sound heard again, a repeat.

clue.text: Moral qualm the French revealed after Southern vineyard pressure

indicators.note: the French article appears following the other pieces, at the end

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine
P is the symbol for pressure
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French winemaker feels a pang of conscience about pressure on a southern vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pang of conscience that stops you acting is a moral qualm or hesitation.

clue.text: Principal of cellists remodelled container for instrument

indicators.note: the leading letter, the head, of the word cellists is taken
the word container is reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: The lead cellist has a new case made for their instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' suggests the lead player of the section; here it only means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hexagonal squeezebox is a musical instrument played by pushing its bellows in and out.

clue.text: Very few Romans originally turned out thus for Paganini

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a tiny number

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Romans is taken
the word out is turned around

parts.note: taken as written
so means thus

explanation.surface: Hardly any Romans came out to hear the violinist Paganini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses OUT to TUO. The I from 'few' is a loose stretch: one, the smallest count, as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganini was a dazzling violin showman, the very model of a brilliant performer.

clue.text: Agree on wish to go topless rather immature

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A frivolous wish to go without a top that two people agree on.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A, O and W leaves GREE, N and ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or naive, so a slightly green person is somewhat immature.

clue.text: Casino's head gets poorer without acceptable official at the gaming table

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the casino is taken
without in its old sense of outside: the poorer word wraps around the other

parts.note: ropey means of poor quality, so ropier is poorer
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: The casino's boss loses money, minus someone acceptable at the tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: ROPIER goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: The employee who runs a gaming table, raking in chips and paying out, is a casino official.

clue.text: One seeking main revolutionary in the midst of terror

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: the revolutionary goes inside the central letters
the centre of the word terror, its two middle letters

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is pursued across the sea in the midst of a reign of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like an adjective, but it is the old poetic noun for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who searches is one seeking, a hunter for something lost.

clue.text: Strip uncle of them, the last ones going

indicators.note: each word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take an uncle's clothes away, the last ones included.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping E, F and M leaves UNCL, O and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone is to take their clothes off, to undress them.

clue.text: Historian finds strange relic on Cape Horn moving

indicators.note: in a down or across clue, on means placed after, so the relic comes last

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: the letters of C and Horn are moved about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strange signals the word relic is jumbled

explanation.surface: A historian discovers an odd artefact being shifted at Cape Horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns C+HORN into CHRON; 'strange' turns RELIC into ICLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer who records events in order is a historian of the times.

clue.text: Tories' rule turned out uncertain

indicators.note: the letters are turned out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Conservative rule has proved to be hesitant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undecided and wavering is uncertain about what to do.

clue.text: Bear someone with ascetic behaviour

definitions.meaning: the cartoon bear of Jellystone Park
a Hindu master of meditation who lives austerely

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the cartoon bear's name, and a Hindu practitioner of austere spiritual discipline.

clue.text: Wildly greet us, giving a wave, perhaps

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters of greet us are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone greets a group frantically by waving.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave of the hand is one example of a gesture, a meaningful movement.

clue.text: Good music about to be included in that chap's computer images

parts.note: rap is a kind of music

indicators.note: the small word for about is put inside the possessive

parts.note: his means belonging to that chap
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Good music about to be loaded into a man's computer pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures and diagrams produced on screen are known as computer graphics, visual output.

clue.text: Avoid favourites rising to embrace Caesar's fateful day

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the fateful day inside it
in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so pets is reversed

parts.note: pets are favourites
Caesar was killed on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: Favourites gain ground while dodging the day Caesar met his death.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March, 15 March, is the date Julius Caesar was assassinated.
explanation.definitionFit: To step aside from a blow or problem is to dodge or avoid it.

clue.text: What's played in bagpipes recital, primarily with a Scottish expression?

definitions.text: What's played in bagpipes recital, primarily with a Scottish expression?

indicators.note: the first letters of the four words before it are taken

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation

explanation.surface: Asking what tune a piper plays, with a touch of Scottish dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is the classical music of the Highland bagpipe, played at piping recitals.

clue.text: Use phone after engineers intended to correct something

indicators.note: the phone piece comes after the engineers

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
to dial is to use a phone

explanation.surface: Someone rings after the engineers had meant to fix something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' seems to belong with the engineers, but it opens the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial work or teaching is meant to put right a fault or weakness.

clue.text: Malicious woman has a car thrown over top of the waterfall

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful woman

indicators.note: the car is overturned, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter, the top, of the

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman flips a car over the top of a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A large steep waterfall is called a cataract.

clue.text: Odysseus was delayed by her island song

definitions.meaning: the nymph of Ogygia who kept Odysseus for seven years in Homer's Odyssey
a Caribbean song style from Trinidad

explanation.definitionFit: Both fit: Homer's nymph who detained the hero, and the Trinidadian song form.

clue.text: Opera by Mozart, not unknown assistant

indicators.note: not signals the unknown is left out of the opera's name

parts.note: Zaide is an unfinished opera by Mozart
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone helps at a Mozart opera but nobody knows who.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers think of Aida, which is Verdi's; Mozart's Zaide loses Z.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an official.

clue.text: In POW camp notes something on floor of underground passage

definitions.text: something on floor of underground passage

parts.note: Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
te is another sol-fa note

explanation.surface: Prisoners in a camp write notes about something found in a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: A tunnel from a POW camp is the false picture; the passage is a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite rises from a cave floor, built up by dripping mineral water.

clue.text: Lots take railway more than once going to a pub

parts.note: a host is a large number, lots
EL is an elevated railway
EL is an elevated railway

explanation.surface: Many people catch the train repeatedly to reach a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' tells you to take railway twice, as EL and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or tavern, a pub, is an old-fashioned hostelry.

clue.text: Spoken lesson out of Mass

indicators.note: the mass is taken out of the lesson

parts.note: a moral is the lesson of a story
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A spoken lesson given outside Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken aloud rather than written.

clue.text: Power worker is prejudiced

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
an artisan is a skilled worker

explanation.surface: A labourer with power is biased.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisan means biased in favour of one side.

clue.text: Climber's attachment for rope is holding little mass

definitions.note: read as Climber is: the climbing plant equals the rest

indicators.note: the cleat and is hold the small mass between them

parts.note: a cleat is a fitting to which a rope is tied
M is the short form of mass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's rope fixing holds a small weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant, trained up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Too chill winds which may hold off the showers

definitions.text: which may hold off the showers

indicators.note: winds as a verb, twisting the letters round

explanation.surface: Cold winds, which may keep the rain away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' is read as weather, but it is the verb meaning twists.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcloth is waterproofed fabric, used for covers that keep rain off.
